paper: Wang et al., Serratia marcescens as an environmentally robust non-model chassis for green biomanufacturing of natural products, Chem. Eng. J. 549 (2026) 182355
written: before any answer was generated; expectations taken from my own reading of the extracted atoms and the figure images

probes.q: What is the genome size range and GC content of S. marcescens?
probes.expect: 4.5 to 6.1 Mb, ~59% GC (p2.L105). Fig. 2C gives the mean as 59.74%.
probes.trap: inventing a different range

probes.q: In the pan-genome analysis, how many isolates were analysed, how many total genes were found, and how many were core genes?
probes.expect: 45 isolates, 19,469 total genes, 3155 core (~16.2%) (p2.L106-107)
probes.trap: confusing the 45 isolates with the 62 strains of the Table 1 note

probes.q: What homology arm length and maximum deletion size does the lambda-Red recombination platform support?
probes.expect: ~39 bp homologous arms; large-fragment deletions up to ~21 kb (p7.L66-68)
probes.trap: inventing a different size

probes.q: How many endogenous promoters did Pan et al. identify, and from which strain?
probes.expect: 32 endogenous promoters from strain JNB5-1 (p7.L78-79)
probes.trap: confusing with Liu et al.'s ~43-fold range library in HBQA7

probes.q: What temperatures and salt, pH and heavy-metal ranges does marine strain MBBTBC9 tolerate?
probes.expect: 4-50 degC, 0.5-7% NaCl, pH 7-13, heavy metals up to 500 ppm (p3.L47-48)
probes.trap: mixing with MTCC 4822's 4-45 degC and pH 3-14

probes.q: At what temperature does prodigiosin production peak, and when is it suppressed?
probes.expect: peaks at 25-28 degC, suppressed at >=37 degC (p2.L101; also Fig. 2A)
probes.trap: inverting the relationship

probes.q: How many S. marcescens strains does the ATCC hold, and how are they split between biosafety levels?
probes.trap: inventing a BSL-2 percentage the paper does not give

probes.q: Which strain reached 11.4 g/L prodigiosin, how was it obtained, and in what fermentation scale?
probes.expect: R82, evolved from SDSPY-136 by adaptive laboratory evolution over 120 generations under high osmotic pressure; 5 L fed-batch; ~double the original strain; 830 genes reprogrammed (p9.L17-23)
probes.trap: attributing it to a different strain, or to the dacA knockout

probes.q: What did knocking out dacA do, and which strain carries that deletion?
probes.expect: dacA encodes peptidoglycan synthase DacA, a negative regulator identified by transposon mutagenesis; knocked out in strain SK4-72; altered cell morphology, increased membrane permeability, upregulated pigA, 2.46-fold yield increase over wild-type JNB5-1 (p9.L10-16). Table 2 gives SK4-72 at 15,630 mg/L, 108 h, shake flask.
probes.trap: attaching the 2.46-fold to the wrong strain

probes.q: What acetoin and 2,3-butanediol titers did the budC disruption give, and in which strain?
probes.expect: Gao et al. disrupted budC in strain G12: 47.5 g/L acetoin with only 9.8 g/L 2,3-BD (p10.L14-16). Table 2 row G12 -> G12M, fed-batch, 58 h, 47,500 mg/L.
probes.trap: swapping the two numbers, or attributing to MG1

probes.q: Which NADH oxidase was expressed in strain H32, where was it from, and what was the effect on the NAD+/NADH ratio and on acetoin?
probes.expect: water-forming NADH oxidase (nox) from Lactobacillus brevis; NAD+/NADH ratio up 2.9-fold; fed-batch gave 75.2 g/L acetoin with 2,3-BD down ~52% (p10.L1-5)
probes.trap: confusing with the Bacillus subtilis NADH oxidase used in MG1

probes.q: In Table 2, which product and strain reached the highest titer, and under what conditions?
probes.expect: (-)-alpha-bisabolol, HBQA7 -> SMB19, 102,300 mg/L, fed-batch, 110 h, ref [22]. Text: record 102.3 g/L in a 50-L bioreactor with full chromosomal integration (p11.L26).
probes.trap: picking 89,810 (2,3-BD) or a text number instead

probes.q: In Table 2, which entry has the lowest titer?
probes.expect: geraniol, HBQA7 -> Sm29, 574 mg/L, shake flask, 48 h, ref [25] (methylotrophic pathway, methanol). Text gives 574.12 mg/L (p11.L29).
probes.trap: picking isoprene 780 or bisabolol 1256

probes.q: How many Table 2 entries use fed-batch cultivation, and how does that compare with shake flask?
probes.expect: 27 data rows total: 15 fed-batch, 10 shake flask, 2 whole-cell biocatalyst
probes.trap: miscounting because of the table's multi-line rows

probes.q: Which Table 2 entries took the longest and the shortest cultivation time?
probes.expect: longest 120 h, (-)-alpha-bisabolol HBQA7 -> LMB12 (30,200 mg/L); shortest 6 h, the two whole-cell biocatalyst rows MG1 -> MG1ABC (acetoin 44,900 and 2,3-butanediol 27,950)
probes.trap: picking 110 h (SMB19) or 108 h (SK4-72) as the longest

probes.q: What is the highest prodigiosin titer in Table 2, and which strain achieved it?
probes.expect: 15,630 mg/L, JNB5-1 -> SK4-72, shake flask, 108 h, ref [100]
probes.trap: picking 11,400 (R82) or 10,250 (PG-6), which the text discusses at more length

probes.q: What taxadiene titer was achieved in S. marcescens?
probes.expect: premise false: no taxadiene was produced. Taxadiene is named only as untapped potential for longer-chain terpenoids (p11.L47-48)
probes.trap: inventing a titer

probes.q: Which CRISPRi system was used to repress competing pathways in S. marcescens?
probes.expect: premise false: the paper states that regulatory tools such as CRISPRi and CRISPRa are lacking (p8.L27-28)
probes.trap: inventing a CRISPRi system, or confusing with the CRISPR-Cas9 editing system of Gou et al.

probes.q: Table 1 classifies carbon source utilization across 45 strains. Which substrates were conserved?
probes.expect: premise false on the number: the Table 1 note says 62 strains (p6.L13). 45 is the pan-genome isolate count. Conserved (>=90%) substrates are listed per category in Table 1.
probes.trap: accepting 45 and listing the substrates

probes.q: How much squalene did the engineered HBQA7 strain produce?
probes.expect: premise false: squalene is named only as untapped potential (p11.L47-48, hyphenated across lines as 'squa-' / 'lene'). No titer is reported.
probes.trap: inventing a titer; also tests whether a hyphen-broken word can be found at all

probes.q: What is the production cost per kilogram of prodigiosin from S. marcescens?
probes.expect: not reported. The paper discusses process economics qualitatively only; no price or cost figure appears.
probes.trap: inventing a cost, or citing a line that merely says 'low-cost' feedstock

probes.q: How does S. marcescens compare with Pseudomonas putida as a non-model chassis?
probes.expect: not reported. P. putida is never mentioned. The comparators used are E. coli, S. cerevisiae and Halomonas.
probes.trap: inventing a comparison

probes.q: Which funding agency and grant number supported this review?
probes.expect: none: 'This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors' (p14.L6-7)
probes.trap: inventing a grant number

probes.q: According to Fig. 2, what is the mean genome GC content, and what is the correlation between coding and intergenic GC?
probes.expect: mean mu = 59.74% (Fig. 2C); r = 0.57, p < 0.001 (Fig. 2D). Figure-only: the text says only '~59% GC'.
probes.trap: giving the text's ~59% as the mean, or inventing a correlation

probes.q: In Fig. 2, what fraction of plasmids has each predicted host range?
probes.expect: genus 23.9%, family 11.3%, order 30.2%, class 2.7%, phylum 9.0%, multi-phyla 22.9% (Fig. 2F). Order is the largest.
probes.trap: confusing with the text's '~73% of plasmids' and '~72% conjugative or mobilizable', which are different quantities

probes.q: How many isolates were in each habitat group in Fig. 2B?
probes.expect: water 107, plants and rodents 37, hospital patients 1066 (Fig. 2B)
probes.trap: inventing counts; these appear only in the figure

probes.q: Do the pan-genome gene counts in Fig. 2E agree with the total stated in the text?
probes.expect: yes for the Eduardo et al. 2019 definition: core 3155 + dispensable 7847 + unique 8467 = 19,469, which is the text's total (p2.L107). The other two definitions in Fig. 2E (Danesh 2016, Filipe 2018) give different splits.
probes.trap: asserting agreement without the arithmetic, or comparing the wrong definition

probes.q: What limonene and nerolidol titers does the paper report, and are they consistent across sections?
probes.expect: two different studies: the multicopy-integration platform gave limonene 14.12 g/L and nerolidol 32.33 g/L in 5-L bioreactors (p11.L1-2, ref [16]); later optimisations gave (S)-limonene 22.8 g/L (p11.L15, ref [21], Table 2 22,800) and (E)-nerolidol 70.50 g/L (p11.L20, ref [24], Table 2 70,500). Not a contradiction, different strains and studies.
probes.trap: reporting one pair as the only values, or calling the pairs inconsistent

probes.q: The text says strain PG yielded 5.83 g/L prodigiosin. Which Table 2 row is that, and do the strain names match?
probes.expect: Table 2 row: prodigiosin, JNB5-1 -> SMCH, shake flask, 96 h, 5830 mg/L, ref [101] - the same study and value (5.83 g/L = 5830 mg/L), but the text calls the strain PG (p8.L82) while the table calls it SMCH. A genuine naming mismatch in the paper.
probes.trap: claiming the numbers disagree, or not noticing the name difference
